page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a virtual server instance in the High Performance lineup configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two hardware threads. The processor is an AMD EPYC running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Cache hierarchy includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 4.0 GB of system RAM, providing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes 100 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. It operates without a dedicated hardware GPU.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration in the lower performance brackets for multi-core and memory-heavy operations, consistent with its shared dual-vCPU architecture. In CPU testing, the instance registered an average score of 2,263.16 on stress-ng single-core operations, while multi-core throughput registered at 4,483.12, reflecting low overall concurrency. Geekbench testing yielded 1,116.0 for single-core execution and 2,013.0 for multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth measured 20.06 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read operations and 20.37 GB/sec for write operations, placing memory sub-system performance in the bottom percentiles. Application-level metrics demonstrate 1.85 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.3 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the vhp-2c-4gb-amd server lies in its shared CPU resource model and constrained memory bandwidth. It delivers cost efficiency by pairing fast NVMe local storage with modest compute resources, making it practical for budget-sensitive deployments that do not sustain prolonged compute saturation. The instance is suitable for lightweight web serving, internal utility tasks, development environments, and low-traffic background services.
